dedupe_keys.name: typhoon haima 2016 priority index and predicted house damage by municipality philippines 510

description: For Typhoon Haima in the Philippines in 2016, the Netherlands Red Cross 510 team predicted which municipalities would be hit worst, using a machine learning model trained on four earlier typhoons, Haiyan, Melor, Hagupit and Rammasun. The first run gave a priority index from 1 to 5; the second run predicted a weighted house damage figure, counting partially damaged houses at 25% of completely damaged ones, and the share of damaged houses among all houses. Inputs were joined per municipality by p-code: government boundaries, the 2015 census, average wind speed and track from University College London, GPM rainfall, poverty from the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program, and houses damaged in past typhoons from the NDRRMC, with roof and wall materials and new geographic features added in the second run. Coverage: Philippine municipalities, using baseline data for the whole country. Access: CSV predictions and Excel feature-importance tables on HDX, with a file comparing models. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: 510 states that absolute numbers of damaged houses and affected people are insufficiently validated and should be used only for further training and ground-truthing, and official NDRRMC counts appear only after local validation. Simulation uses are an early example of impact-based forecasting of housing damage, and a benchmark for typhoon damage models. Related records: the Philippines pre-disaster indicators and TM Open Buildings.
